correctness.rationale: Gaussian radial factorization independently recovers the sphere moments. For a standard Gaussian vector G, the quadratic-form generating function is det(I−2zA)^(-1/2), and inserting (u·G)^2 multiplies it by uᵀ(I−2zA)^(-1)u. Dividing the resulting moments by the appropriate radial moments and using tr(A^4)=(tr(A²))²/2 gives the frozen mixed and pure terms. Odd-parity terms vanish. For each eigenvalue λ, the remaining two eigenvalues contribute at least λ²/2 to tr(A²); equality forces both equal. The real deficit and optimizer s/(s+t)=15/32 follow, and alignment with the unique simple eigenline is necessary since both degree energies are positive. On that axis the normalized linear and P2 coefficients are the square roots of 3·15/32 and 5·17/32; sign and phase are absorbed by axis reversal and scaling. In the complex case Cauchy–Schwarz forces squared real and imaginary parts to be proportional when both are nonzero. The sphere is connected and the parts are real analytic, so the product of the sum and difference being identically zero forces one factor to vanish identically. This exhausts equality. Independent symbolic moment and square completion checks replay with `python /workspace/replay_frozen_reviews.py 1`; those calculations verify identities, not the equality logic by enumeration.
